Help & Support
Popular questions
How do points & streaks work?

You earn points from the daily quiz and games. Play every day to keep your streak — miss a day and it resets, but your XP and badges always stay.

How do I unlock Premium?

Tap any 🔒 feature and choose "Ask my guardian to unlock". Your grown-up gets a link and can subscribe with mobile money (MTN or Airtel).

Is ZedExams safe for my child?

Yes — there's no chatting between children anywhere, a guardian approves the account, and Ask Zed is child-safe with a report button.

Can I use it offline?

Yes. Save papers and notes for offline, and your daily lessons work without data. Ask Zed and live challenges need the internet.

Why do I only see my grade?

ZedExams shows your grade's lessons, papers and games so you practise exactly what your exam covers.

Your study helper · online
Hi Milton! 👋 I'm Zed. Ask me anything about your Grade 7 topics and I'll explain it simply. What are you learning today?
Why do we use "because" and not "so"?
Good question! 🌟 Because gives the reason, and so gives the result.

• I stayed home because it was raining. (reason)
• It was raining, so I stayed home. (result)

Same idea — the joining word just changes where the reason goes. Want to try one? 😊

Part 2: Each question contains a sentence from which a word or group of words is missing. Choose the word or group of words that makes the sentence right.

21. I enjoyed the play …… I have seen it before.

A  after     B  and     C  although     D  but

22. Zacheus climbed a tree to see Jesus …… he was short.

A  and     B  because     C  but     D  yet

23. I received an …… Award from the University of Zambia last year.

A  Huonarary     B  Honuorary     C  Honorary     D  Hunarary

24. The …… could hardly hear the speech because of the music from a nearby market.

A  odience     B  uadience     C  audience     D  awdience

25. We went to the ……

A  markit.     B  market.     C  marcket.     D  markat.

Part 3: Questions 26 – 30
In each question, there are four sentences that are almost the same, but only one has the correct punctuation mark. Choose the sentence which is correctly punctuated.

26.

A  She has a beautiful voice.
B  She has a beautiful voice,
C  she has a beautiful voice.
D  She has a beautiful voice?

27.

A  The children are playing outside?
B  The children are playing outside;
C  The children are playing outside
D  The children are playing outside.

28.

A  Plums, pears, apples and bananas are good sources of vitamin C?
B  Plums pears apples and bananas are good sources of vitamin C.
C  Plums, pears, apples and bananas are good sources of vitamin C.
D  Plums, pears, apples and bananas are good sources of Vitamin C,

Page 2 of 3  ·  PSME/English Language/PRISCA/2026

Part 4: Questions 31 – 40
Read the passage below carefully, then answer the questions that follow.

Mwansa woke up very early on the day of the market. The sun had not yet risen over the hills of Kasama, and the air was cool and quiet. She helped her mother pack the baskets of vegetables — tomatoes, rape and fresh beans from their garden…

31. Where does this story take place?

A  Lusaka     B  Kasama     C  Ndola     D  Choma

32. What did Mwansa help her mother to do?

A  cook breakfast     B  fetch water
C  pack vegetables     D  sweep the yard

ENGLISH · TERM 2 · STRUCTURE
Conjunctions — the joining words 🔗
7 min read · 3 sections · with Zed
💡 Tap any purple word to see how to use it, with extra examples.

A conjunction is a joining word. It works like glue — it sticks two words or two sentences together to make one longer, smoother sentence.

Zed's map: there are 3 families of joining words. Let's meet them one by one — with a little game in each! 🎮
1 Coordinating — joining equals
🔑 KEY POINTS
and adds · but contrast · or choice · so result · yet surprise contrast. Both sides of the sentence are equal.

These join words or sentences of equal importance — two ideas that could each stand on their own.

andadds information
butshows contrast
orshows a choice
soshows a result
yetan unexpected contrast
Mutale went to the market. + She bought tomatoes.
→ Mutale went to the market and bought tomatoes. ✨
Bwalya was tired. He kept on studying.
Which joining word fits best?
👆 Tap to see the answer
Bwalya was tired but he kept on studying. 💪
The two ideas fight each other — so we use but.
✏️ YOUR TURN
I like mangoes …… I do not like lemons.
🎯 SECTION CHECK — Coordinating
It started raining, …… we ran inside.
Let's look at it again
so shows a result. The rain is the reason — running inside is what happened because of it.
I was hungry, so I ate my nshima.
The sun was hot, so we sat under the mango tree.
Try a similar one: The test was easy, …… everyone passed.
2 Subordinating — one idea depends on the other
🔑 KEY POINTS
Join a main clause to a dependent clause. because = why · if/unless = condition · when/while/before/after/since = time · although = surprise.

These join a main clause to a dependent clause — one part of the sentence leans on the other, telling us why, when or on what condition.

because although if when while before after since unless

Chipo stayed at home because she was sick.
Although it was raining, we continued playing.
Wash your hands before you eat.
✏️ YOUR TURN
Zacheus climbed a tree …… he was short.
✏️ YOUR TURN
The learners became quiet …… the teacher entered.
🎯 SECTION CHECK — Subordinating
…… you study hard, you will pass the exam.
Let's look at it again
if sets a condition — the passing depends on the studying. One part of the sentence leans on the other.
If you water the plant, it will grow.
You will be late unless you hurry. (unless = if you do not)
Try a similar one: You will miss the bus …… you run.
3 Conjunction pairs — words that work as a team
🔑 KEY POINTS
either … or · neither … nor · both … and · not only … but also. Pairs always travel together — see one, expect its partner.

Some conjunctions are always used in pairs. If you see the first one, its partner must follow!

either … or neither … nor both … and not only … but also

Both Chanda and Mutale passed the test.
Not only did it rain, but it also hailed.
✏️ YOUR TURN
Neither Bwalya …… Chipo was late for class.
🎯 SECTION CHECK — Conjunction pairs
…… only did Mwansa sing, but she also danced.
Let's look at it again
The pair is not only … but also. When you see but also later in the sentence, its partner not only must come first. Pairs always travel together!
Not only is Zed clever, but he is also friendly.
Either you come now, or we leave.
Try a similar one: …… Chanda or Taonga will bring the ball.
Exam alert! Conjunction questions appear in every Grade 7 English paper — like Part 2 of the 2026 paper you practised. Master these and those marks are yours.

SCIENCE · THE HUMAN BODY
The Digestive System 🍽️
8 min read · tap the organs · with Zed

Digestion is the breaking down of food into tiny nutrients that your body cells can use for energy and growth.

The digestive system is also called the alimentary canal or gut. It runs all the way from the mouth to the anus.

👆 The food's journey — top to bottom
STARTS IN
👄 Mouth
→
ENDS IN
🌀 Small intestine

Digestion starts in the mouth (chewing) and is completed in the small intestine, where the nutrients are taken into the blood. The large intestine after it only takes back water — the food is already digested by then.

Tap any organ below to see a real picture and find out what it does! 🔍
1 The organs of digestion
Mouth (teeth & tongue)
Gullet (Esophagus)
Stomach
Liver
Gall bladder
Pancreas
Small intestine
Large intestine
2 Helper organs 🤝

Some organs are not part of the food tube — food never passes through them — but they still help digestion by making special juices. We call them helper organs.

💧
Salivary glands
make saliva in the mouth
🟥
Liver
makes bile to break down fats
🟢
Gall bladder
stores the bile until it is needed
🟡
Pancreas
makes juices (enzymes) for the small intestine

💡 The food tube itself is: mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus.

3 The journey of food
1
Mouth — teeth chew, saliva softens
▼
2
Esophagus — pushes food down to the stomach
▼
3
Stomach — churns food into a paste
▼
4
Small intestine — digestion completed; food absorbed into blood
▼
5
Large intestine — water & minerals absorbed
▼
6
Undigested food — leaves the body as waste
Remember the two jobs: the small intestine grabs the nutrients; the large intestine grabs the water.
4 Label the diagram ✏️

Drag each word onto the right box — or tap a word, then tap a box. Just like the exam!

5 Words to know 📖
Ingestiontaking food into the mouth
Gastric juicestomach juice that breaks down proteins
Bile juicefrom the liver; breaks down fats & oils
Egestionreleasing faeces through the anus (voiding)
🎯 SECTION CHECK
Which organ absorbs the nutrients from food?
Let's look again
The small intestine is a long coiled tube. As food passes through it slowly, the nutrients soak into the blood. The large intestine comes after, and it takes the water.
Try again: The large intestine mainly absorbs ……
🎯 SECTION CHECK
Which of these is a HELPER organ (food does not pass through it)?
Let's look again
Food travels through the stomach and gullet — they are part of the food tube. But it never passes through the liver; the liver just sends in bile to help. That makes it a helper organ.
Try again: The pancreas is a helper organ because it ……
